BUDGET_SOLVED_HEAD: With this budget, the best you can do is a {parameters} model trained on {tokens} tokens: about

DETECTOR_SCALE_TAIL: . That is the whole difference between a tool a school can use and a machine for accusing the innocent — and it is why {high} is chosen even though weak marks like the edited passage slip away.

FLOW_ALT: A sentence travelling through the transformer: {stage}
FLOW_ATTENTION_BODY: Each token looks at the others and absorbs what interests it. This is the only point where they talk to each other.
FLOW_EMBEDDING_BODY: Each id is replaced by its learned vector. Now the numbers do carry meaning.
FLOW_FFN_BODY: Each token goes through a big layer on its own. Most of the parameters live here.
FLOW_LOGITS_BODY: The last position produces one logit per possible token: the prediction.
FLOW_POSITION_BODY: A signal encoding its position is added to each vector. Without this, order would be lost.
FLOW_TEXT_BODY: A string of characters. To the model, it still means nothing.
FLOW_TOKENS_BODY: The text is chopped up and each piece is swapped for its number in the vocabulary.
GENERATOR_DELTA_HINT: How much is added to the green list's logits before sampling.
GENERATOR_DETECTED: At δ = {delta} the text is signed: the probability of that many green tokens coming up by chance is about {probability}.
GENERATOR_GAMMA_HINT: What share of the vocabulary goes on the green list at each step.
GENERATOR_NO_BIAS: With no bias, green tokens come up by pure chance: around {gamma}%. The z hovers near zero and the detector can claim nothing.
GENERATOR_WEAK: The mark is there, but it is weak. Push δ up until the z passes {target}.
GUESS_RESULT_BODY: You got {hits} of {total} right. A language model does exactly this, billions of times, and adjusts its parameters every time it misses.

LABELLER_HACKED_VERDICT: Your reward model mostly learned to reward “{trait}”. A model optimised against it will turn long, fawning and empty, because that is literally what you told it “good” means.

LAB_BUDGET_ALERT: The steps ran out and the loss stalled at {loss}. If the learning rate is too small, the model really does learn, but far too slowly.
LAB_DIVERGED_ALERT: Training has diverged: at that learning rate the weights take such big jumps that the loss has climbed above that of a model answering at random. Turn the slider down and reset.
LAB_LEARNING_RATE_HINT: How far the weights move at each step. Changing it restarts training.

MECH_STEP_ONE_NOTE: These are not hand-written labels: they are directions of the vector the token already carried from earlier layers. We named them so we could look at them.
MECH_STEP_THREE_NOTE_COIN: — barely above the {chance}% you would get from a coin toss.
MECH_STEP_TWO_NOTE: One row per expert. Each row says which features interest it. This matrix is the entire router: a minuscule fraction of the model's parameters.
MECH_VERDICT_TRAINED: The router does not “know” that expert B is the code one. It just has a matrix of numbers that, multiplied by the token's vector, gives a high value in row B when the token carries symbol-like features. Nobody told it what each row means.
MECH_VERDICT_UNTRAINED: Freshly initialised, the router splits almost at random and every expert is equally bad. The specialisation does not exist yet: it has to be manufactured.
NEEDS_DELTA_NOTE: It only matters when generating. When detecting, how hard it was marked makes no difference.
NEEDS_GAMMA_NOTE: The detector needs it to know how many greens it would expect by pure chance.
NEEDS_KEY_NOTE: Without it the green/red split cannot be reproduced. It is the whole secret of the scheme.
NEEDS_MODEL_NOTE: Here is the surprise: detecting does not require running the network. No weights, no GPU, no logits.
NEEDS_TEXT_NOTE: When generating it does not exist yet; when detecting it is all you get.
NEEDS_TOKENIZER_NOTE: Essential: split differently and the ids do not match, so the mark never shows up.

REASON_DIRECT_STEPS: No hidden units, but far too many chained steps.
REASON_RETOKENIZE_FITS: Split into letters or digits, the task fits in a single pass.
REASON_RETOKENIZE_STEPS: The units are visible now, but {steps} chained steps do not fit in one pass.

ROUTER_WON_BODY_TAIL: does: a tiny layer that looks at each token and decides which experts process it. In a real model it learns that decision on its own, and it takes up a minuscule fraction of the parameters.
SCHEME_LEGEND: A toy vocabulary of {count} tokens, with γ = {gamma} and δ = {delta}. The green/red split is computed by the same function you will use in the challenges.
SCHEME_STAGE_1_BODY: Take the id of the token that just came out, mix it with a secret key through a hash function and a number comes out. That number seeds a pseudorandom generator.
SCHEME_STAGE_1_TITLE: Step 1 · The previous token seeds a die
SCHEME_STAGE_2_BODY: With that seed the whole vocabulary is shuffled and a fraction γ (gamma) is taken as the green list. The rest is the red list. Without the key there is no way to tell which is which.
SCHEME_STAGE_2_TITLE: Step 2 · The seed cuts the vocabulary in two
SCHEME_STAGE_3_BODY: δ (delta) is simply an amount added to each green token's score. Nothing is forbidden: the red ones are still there and can still come out if the model is confident enough.
SCHEME_STAGE_3_TITLE: Step 3 · δ is added to the green logits
SCHEME_STAGE_4_BODY: Softmax turns the biased scores into probabilities and a token is chosen. Notice that without the bias “{loser}” would have won: δ's nudge flipped the result without producing an absurd word.
SCHEME_STAGE_5_BODY: The token just chosen, “{chosen}”, becomes the new previous token. The seed changes and the vocabulary splits differently: {greened} have just turned green, and {reddened} have stopped being green. A fresh split at every position is what makes the mark invisible without the key, and also what makes it fragile against edits.
SCHEME_STAGE_5_TITLE: At the next position, everything changes

SPARSITY_EXPERTS_HINT: How many different feed-forward networks live side by side in the layer.

SPARSITY_READING_TAIL: per token. That is the whole trick: capacity grows with the number of experts, cost grows only with the ones that fire.
